Chapter.Content: 18 — ECS contracts, diagnostics, and GPU handoff
Reading map · Previous chapter · Next chapter

An ECS needs evidence for its identity, query, and memory promises before rendering can consume its state. This chapter closes those defenses and transitions from world storage to explicit GPU work and resource lifetimes.
By the end: Audit ECS invariants with diagnostics and tests, then explain how entity data becomes render work with explicit ownership.

Content.Strong: But smallest pool is not always absolute optimality

Chapter.Content: Imagine smallest pool is randomly ordered relative to other component dense arrays, causing many cache misses.
A slightly larger pool whose order correlates with another hot pool might sometimes outperform it.
Archetype storage solves much of this by aligning component row ownership.
Therefore smallest-pool is a strong sparse-set heuristic, not a universal theorem about machine performance.

Chapter.Content: The largest architectural lesson is that an entity, a component object, the component’s memory address, the authored scene object, the physics body, the renderer object and the network object are all different identities with different lifetimes. Good engine architecture connects those identities with explicit bridges rather than pretending one integer or pointer can safely mean all of them.
